jobs.title: Global Program Manager-Contingent Workforce Program & Governance
jobs.description:
PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.

Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking.  We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.

Role Overview

PIMCO is seeking a highly experienced Global Program Manager to lead the firm's contingent workforce program globally. This role serves as the end-to-end process owner for contingent worker engagement, contract governance, supplier management, operational execution, compliance oversight, and technology enablement.

The successful candidate will partner closely with Legal, Finance, Technology, Human Resources, and business stakeholders to ensure contingent workforce engagements are managed consistently, efficiently, and in compliance with all applicable legal, regulatory, and policy requirements across jurisdictions.

This role combines operational excellence, risk management, vendor governance, and technology administration to deliver a scalable, best-in-class contingent workforce program.

Key Responsibilities

Global Contingent Workforce Program Management
- Serve as the global process owner for PIMCO's contingent workforce program.
- Manage the full lifecycle of contingent worker engagements, including but not limited to: - Intake and sourcing requests
- Interview coordination
- Business approvals as needed
- Contract initiation and execution
- Worker onboarding
- Profile setup and system provisioning
- Assignment extensions and modifications
- Offboarding and termination activities

- Develop and maintain a globally consistent operating model for contingent workforce management.
- Drive continuous improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, governance, risk mitigation, and user experience.

Contract Management and Procurement Governance
- Draft, negotiate, and administer contingent workforce contracts globally.
- Manage a diverse portfolio of workforce-related agreements, including: - Staffing agency agreements
- Statement of Work (SOW) engagements
- Managed service provider (MSP) arrangements
- Independent consultant agreements
- Professional services and consulting contracts

- Partner with Legal to ensure contracts appropriately address regulatory, co-employment, data privacy, confidentiality, intellectual property, and risk considerations.
- Establish and maintain contract standards, templates, and governance frameworks.

Vendor and Supplier Management
- Serve as the primary relationship manager for contingent workforce suppliers and service providers.
- Conduct supplier performance reviews and business assessments.
- Monitor vendor compliance, service levels, contract obligations, and operational performance.
- Support procurement-driven sourcing and competitive bidding activities when appropriate.
- Drive supplier rationalization and cost optimization initiatives.

Compliance and Risk Management
- Partner with Legal and Compliance to develop and maintain contingent workforce policies and procedures.
- Identify, assess, and mitigate contingent workforce risks.
- Maintain governance controls that support audit readiness and regulatory compliance.
- Lead remediation efforts for identified compliance gaps and operational risks.

Technology and Systems Administration
- Manage and oversee the Contingent Worker Hub and Beeline platforms with associated workflow tools.
- Administer contingent worker lifecycle transactions and maintain records, including: - Profile creation
- Data maintenance
- Assignment extensions
- Worker transfers
- Terminations
- Access-related updates

- Partner with Technology teams to optimize system configurations, integrations, automation, and reporting capabilities.
- Leverage platforms such as Workday, ServiceNow, vendor management systems (VMS), and procurement technologies to improve operational effectiveness. The firm's contingent worker processes utilize Beeline, ServiceNow, and Workday-integrated workflows for onboarding, extensions, data changes, and terminations.

Operational Excellence and Case Management
- Manage day-to-day contingent workforce case management operational activities and escalations through ServiceNow and Beeline.
- Establish service-level agreements (SLAs), performance metrics, and operational controls.
- Ensure timely completion of onboarding, extensions, data changes, and terminations.
- Monitor operational KPIs and identify opportunities for automation and process simplification.
- Support audit requests, reporting requirements, and management reviews.

Knowledge Management and Process Governance
- Own and maintain all contingent workforce process documentation, knowledge articles, training materials, and operating procedures.
- Ensure knowledge bases remain current, accurate, and aligned with policy requirements.
- Develop manager-facing guidance and self-service resources.
- Drive standardization and continuous process improvement across regions and business units.

Stakeholder Communication and Change Management
- Provide education on contingent workforce policies, procedures, and compliance requirements.
- Lead change management efforts associated with program enhancements, technology implementations, and policy updates.
- Act as a trusted advisor to business leaders regarding contingent workforce strategy and governance.

Qualifications

Required Experience
- 5-10+ years of experience in Strategic Sourcing, Vendor Management, Workforce Management, Operations, or a related field.
- Extensive experience managing contingent workforce programs in a global organization.
- Deep expertise in contingent workforce contracting, supplier governance, and risk management.
- Experience negotiating complex agreements across multiple jurisdictions.
- Strong understanding of co-employment risk, worker classification, labor regulations, and contingent workforce compliance.
- Experience partnering with Legal, Finance, Technology, Human Resources, and business stakeholders.
- Experience developing and implementing scalable operational processes and governance frameworks.

Technical Skills
- Knowledge of: - Vendor Management Systems (VMS)
- Contract lifecycle management platforms
- Procurement and sourcing tools
- Systems (Workday, ServiceNow)

- Strong reporting and analytical capabilities.
- Experience with workflow automation and process optimization initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree in Business, Supply Chain, Procurement, Finance, or related discipline.
- Master's degree preferred.
- Professional certifications such as: - CPSM (Certified Professional in Supply Management)
- CIPS (Chartered Institute of Procurement & Supply)
- Certified Contingent Workforce Professional (CCWP)

Position Description
PIMCO’s Alternative Funds platform totals approximately $150 billion across multiple strategies and vehicle structures, including evergreen and closed-ended funds.   The Alternatives Funds Finance Team is responsible for end-to-end financial oversight across the platform, including financial accounting and control, investor reporting, tax structuring and compliance, treasury and liquidity management, operations, and oversight of investment partners and third-party service providers.   The team works closely and cross-functionally with Portfolio Management, Product Strategy, Account Management, Legal, Tax, and Operations, and reports into the Executive Office

The Alternative Funds Finance Team is seeking to add a high-caliber, intellectual curious professional with strong investment company and alternative asset accounting experience to the Financial Control team. This individual will be responsible for the financial control and deal execution oversight of a subset of private credit and closed-ended alternatives funds.   Working closely with the existing team, the Alternatives Fund Finance Manager will help design and execute an effective oversight model to ensure accurate, timely, and high-quality financial reporting for all internal and external constituents of this fund group.

While this role includes core financial accounting and reporting responsibilities, it is embedded in the investment lifecycle and extends beyond traditional controller activities.   The individual will play an active role in ensuring complex investment activity is appropriately structured, executed, book, and reported accurately, partnering closely with Portfolio Management, Legal, Tax, Treasury, Operations, and third‑party service providers throughout the transaction process.

A significant component of this role involves hands-on oversight of illiquid private investments across a diverse asset class mix, including commercial and residential real estate debt and equity, bank loans, asset-backed and other specialty finance structured products, subordinated debt, and preferred and common equity in privately held companies, as well as fixed income, derivatives, and other unique securities. The role requires a strong understanding of close-ended and hybrid fund structures, including blocker structures, as well as the judgment and influence to operate effectively across numerous stakeholders and concurrent transactions.

As the PIMCO Alternatives business continues to grow and evolve, this is a unique opportunity to join a high-performing, highly collaborative team that sits close to the investment decision-making process and plays a meaningful role in bringing complex transactions to life.

- Manage fund-level treasury and liquidity activities, including cash flow forecasting, capital calls, distributions, and coordination with the financing team); prepare analysis related to investment pipeline and liquidity planning.

jobs.title: People Operations Analyst - 12 Month FTC
jobs.description:
PIMCO is a global leader in active fixed income with deep expertise across public and private markets. We invest our clients’ capital across a range of fixed income and credit opportunities, leveraging our decades of experience navigating complex debt markets. Our flexible capital base and deep relationships with issuers have helped us become one of the world’s largest providers of traditional and nontraditional solutions for companies that need financing and investors who seek strong risk-adjusted returns.

Since 1971, our people have shaped our organization through a high-performance inclusive culture, in which we celebrate diverse thinking.  We invest in our people and strive to imprint our CORE values of Collaboration, Openness, Responsibility and Excellence. We believe each of us is here to help others succeed and this has led to PIMCO being recognized as an innovator, industry thought leader and trusted advisor to our clients.

Role Overview
The People Operations Analyst is an early-career role for someone interested in helping build the future of People Operations. The Analyst will deliver accurate, responsive and employee-centered HR services while using technology, data, knowledge and continuous improvement practices to make those services simpler, more scalable and easier to navigate.

This role combines hands-on operational delivery with future-focused problem solving. The Analyst will support employee inquiries and lifecycle processes, identify recurring issues and friction, partner with subject matter experts to clarify rules and exceptions, and help translate operational needs into improved processes, knowledge, self-service and responsible AI or automation use cases.
Success requires strong attention to detail, sound judgment, curiosity and a willingness to learn. The ideal candidate can operate within established controls while also asking thoughtful questions, navigating ambiguity and contributing ideas that improve the employee experience and the way People Operations delivers its work.

What You Will Do
Employee and Manager Support
- Respond to employee and manager inquiries with empathy, accuracy and appropriate urgency across HR policies, processes and programs.

- Manage cases through the HR service management platform, document actions clearly and support delivery against service expectations.

- Research issues, distinguish routine questions from exceptions and escalate sensitive or higher-risk matters appropriately.

- Look beyond case closure to understand the employee need, remove confusion where possible and create a consistent service experience.

Employee Lifecycle Operations
- Execute and coordinate core employee lifecycle activities, including onboarding, transfers, mobility, changes and offboarding.
- Complete HR transactions and documentation accurately, maintaining data integrity, confidentiality, compliance and audit-ready records.
- Coordinate across People Operations, HR Business Partners, Subject Matter Experts, and other partners to support timely outcomes.
- Identify unclear handoffs, recurring delays or process gaps and raise practical recommendations for improvement.

Digital Enablement, AI and Automation
- Use approved AI and digital tools to support research, drafting, summarization, analysis and operational delivery, with appropriate human review.
- Identify repetitive, manual or high-friction activities that may benefit from standardization, self-service, automation or AI enablement.
- Help define practical use cases by documenting the business problem, users, process, required data, risks, controls and desired outcome.
- Participate in testing new tools and workflows, document findings and provide clear feedback on accuracy, usability and employee impact.
- Apply sound judgment regarding confidential information, data quality, bias, accuracy and when human or subject matter expert review is required.
- Stay curious about emerging tools and share relevant, practical ideas that could improve People Operations.

Process Improvement and Operational Insight
- Review workflows, case themes, employee feedback and available service data to identify root causes and improvement opportunities.
- Map current processes, clarify decision points and exceptions, and help design simpler and more consistent ways of working.
- Contribute to process documentation, standard operating procedures, controls and measurement approaches.
- Support implementation of improvements and assess whether changes reduced effort, improved quality or created a better employee experience.

Knowledge Management and Self-Service
- Create, update and maintain clear, accurate and accessible knowledge articles for employees, managers and HR colleagues.
- Partner with subject matter experts to translate policies and specialist knowledge into practical guidance, decision logic and employee-friendly content.
- Identify knowledge gaps based on recurring inquiries and recommend content or self-service improvements.
- Help ensure knowledge remains current, consistent across channels and aligned with global standards and regional requirements.

Partnership and Navigation of Ambiguity
- Build effective working relationships across People Operations and with HR and business partners.
- Approach unfamiliar or ambiguous situations by gathering facts, identifying what is known and unknown, assessing risk and proposing a path forward.
- Engage subject matter experts with focused questions and relevant context rather than simply passing work to another team.
- Balance employee experience, consistency, speed, risk and practicality when evaluating options.
- Know when to act independently, when to seek guidance and when escalation is required.

Employee Experience and Service Excellence
- Consider the employee and manager experience at each stage of a process, including the clarity, accessibility and tone of communications.
- Listen for signals of confusion or frustration and use them to improve processes, knowledge and service delivery.
- Communicate clearly and professionally, including when an answer is not immediate or a request cannot be fulfilled as expected.
- Contribute to a service culture grounded in ownership, responsiveness, respect and continuous improvement.

What You Bring
Required Qualifications
- Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience in human resources, business, information systems, analytics, operations, psychology or another relevant field.

- Strong attention to detail and commitment to accurate, high-quality work.

- Demonstrated curiosity about technology, AI, automation or new ways of working, including the ability to learn unfamiliar tools quickly.

- Structured problem-solving skills and the ability to break an unclear issue into manageable questions and next steps.

- Clear written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain information simply and adapt to different audiences.

- Sound judgment, discretion and respect for confidential and sensitive information.

- Service orientation, and empathy for employees and managers navigating HR processes.

- Ability to organize competing priorities, roll up your sleeves type, follow through on commitments and work effectively in a fast-paced environment.

- Ability to collaborate with colleagues from different areas of expertise and incorporate feedback.

Preferred Qualifications
- Experience in HR operations, shared services, customer service, business operations, process improvement, analytics or a technology-enabled service environment.
- Exposure to HR platforms or workflow tools such as Workday, ServiceNow, case management, knowledge management or reporting solutions.
- Experience using generative AI, automation, data or digital tools to improve a project, service, workflow or user experience.
- Coursework, projects, internships or extracurricular experience spanning both people or service topics and technology, analytics or process design.
- Experience creating clear guidance, documenting a process, analyzing recurring issues or working with a subject matter expert.
